text.title: Business Model Research Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether any paid observation exists to score against, whether more than one model is genuinely available to choose between, and whether a candidate carries non-payers — to full application, a cost-to-serve-first path, or a skip that names the methodology to run instead.

decision-tree.root-question: Has anyone paid for this product or a close comparable, so at least one observed CAC or ARPA figure exists for the comparison to rest on?

branch.when: zero paid observations — no one has bought this or a close comparable, so every CAC, ARPA and churn cell would be an assumption

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to business-model-planning to design a model and to the tests that would produce a first price signal — a scoring table over pure assumptions lends the author's prior a precision the data cannot carry

branch.when: only one model is actually available — a marketplace take rate or app-store billing rules dictate the metric — or the real question is a single price point on a model already chosen

conclusion.verdict: skip; there is no candidate set to rank — route to pricing-strategy for a price point, or to business-model-planning if the model itself is still open

branch.when: two or more candidate models are genuinely available and paid observations exist for at least one
branch.question: Does any candidate carry users who consume the product without paying — a free tier, a free trial, or a freemium path?

branch.when: yes; at least one candidate serves non-payers

conclusion.verdict: apply, and no such row enters `ranked_models` without an explicit free-user cost-to-serve line in the margin cell plus a sourced free-to-paid conversion rate and the traffic it implies

branch.when: no; every candidate is paid from first use

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; one customer unit and one period declared once and applied to every row, churn compounded rather than multiplied, and the LTV:CAC and payback gates applied before anything is ranked, with failing models left visible
